technical.lead: US export-control order forces Anthropic to disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5
technical.body: Anthropic cut off worldwide access to its two most capable models, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, after the US government issued an export-control directive at 5:21pm ET on June 12 citing national-security authorities. The order bars access by any foreign national inside or outside the US, including Anthropic's own foreign-national staff, which the company says forces it to disable both models for every customer to stay compliant; all other Claude models remain available. The stated basis is a jailbreaking method against Fable 5, but Anthropic says it was shown only verbal evidence of a narrow, non-universal technique that surfaces a few previously known minor vulnerabilities by asking the model to read a codebase and identify flaws — a capability it notes is widely available from rival models including OpenAI's GPT-5.5. Landing three days after the June 9 general-availability launch, it is the first time a US directive has forced a frontier lab to recall a generally available commercial model, and Anthropic warned that applying this standard industry-wide would essentially halt all new frontier-model deployments.

technical.lead: Moonshot ships open-weight Kimi K2.7-Code, but every benchmark is self-reported
technical.body: Moonshot AI released Kimi K2.7-Code on June 12, an open-weight coding-specialized model published to Hugging Face under a Modified MIT license. It is a 1-trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts design (about 32B active across 384 experts) with a 256K-token context window, tuned for long-horizon agentic software engineering, and Moonshot says it uses roughly 30% fewer reasoning tokens than K2.6 while scoring higher: a reported +21.8% on Kimi Code Bench v2, +11.0% on Program Bench, +31.5% on MLS Bench Lite, and 81.1 on MCP Mark Verified, at $0.95/$4.00 per million input/output tokens under model id kimi-k2.7-code. The claims drew immediate skepticism because every headline number comes from Moonshot's own in-house suites, with no independent results yet on the public benchmarks practitioners trust (SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench, LiveCodeBench, GPQA Diamond, AIME, MMLU-Pro) — a reminder that a same-week drop with only self-reported wins should be treated as provisional until external runs land.

technical.lead: OWASP agentic-AI report ties prompt injection to a cataloged CVE record
technical.body: OWASP published State of Agentic AI Security and Governance v2.01 on June 11, reworking last year's largely theoretical guidance into a record tied to real CVEs, vendor advisories and breach reports. Prompt injection is positioned as the dominant attack vector, mapped to six of the ten categories in OWASP's Top 10 for Agentic Applications, on the basis that an LLM cannot separate system instructions, user input and external data within a single token stream; the report leans on Simon Willison's lethal trifecta and Meta's Agents Rule of Two as mitigation framings. Coding agents are now the center of agentic risk: of 53 tracked projects, 28 are coding agents, and a new Real-World Incidents tracker ties concrete failures to specific entries, citing the MCP RCE CVE-2025-6514 (CVSS 9.6), the Cursor environment-poisoning flaw CVE-2026-22708, an OpenAI Codex CLI sandbox bypass (CVE-2025-59532), and the March 2026 LiteLLM backdoor that shipped an autonomous attack bot in roughly 47,000 downloads over a three-hour window.

technical.lead: Oracle's $95B fiscal-2027 capex guide drags the semiconductor complex
technical.body: An AI-spending scare hit the semiconductor complex on June 11: Oracle fell about 8.9% after-hours when it guided to as much as $95 billion in capital expenditure for fiscal 2027, up from $55.66 billion in fiscal 2026, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index dropped 3.57% to 12,206.46 with Nvidia and Broadcom among the heaviest weights on the S&P 500. The reaction came despite Oracle's own strong print (revenue up about 21% and cloud-infrastructure revenue up 93% to $5.8 billion), crystallizing a shift in investor focus from whether AI demand is real to how the buildout gets funded — as eMarketer's Jacob Bourne put it, the demand is real but the funding question is getting harder, not easier. TSMC offered a counterweight, reporting May revenue of NT$416.98 billion, up 30.1% year over year.

technical.lead: Huawei rebuilds HarmonyOS 7 around an OS-level on-device agent runtime
technical.body: At its Developer Conference on June 12, Huawei unveiled HarmonyOS 7 and released a developer beta, with the headline change being a shift of HarmonyOS Intelligence into a full agent architecture via the new HarmonyOS Agent Framework 2.0. Huawei frames the model as Intention as Service, compressing multi-step operations into a single conversation through task decomposition, tool calling and autonomous execution, and claims a task-execution success rate above 90% plus a roughly 15% performance uplift over HarmonyOS 6.1. The OS spans phones, tablets, PCs, wearables and IoT, connecting to a large catalog of specialized agents, with the official release slated for this fall. It is a notable embedded-system signal: an OS-level agent runtime baked into the device platform rather than bolted on as an app.
